improvement_path.rationale: A cheap inspection can establish whether the deployed backend selects FlashInfer CuTeDSL MegaMoE and whether decode workspace selection is already active. If eligible, measuring MegaMoE decode time alongside KV capacity gives a testable path to serving value. The B200 bottleneck and effect size are unknown.

legal_correct_integration.rationale: The proposed global capacity agreement, fixed-workspace fallback, idle-rank participation, unequal and zero-rank tests, and DSpark token-bound check address the stated hazards. The active backend, required FlashInfer APIs, actual token bound, and complete workspace implementation are not established.

source_support.rationale: PR #62073 makes the author claim that the smaller workspace is used when “every DP rank's batch fits,” and reports a Beam prefill result on four GB300s. H1 incorrectly says that PR reports no decode gain. “decode/draft are essentially unchanged” comes from PR #57604 about different staging and gather changes. The supplied code excerpt does not show the workspace branch.

controlled_experiment.rationale: The design compares within R7b two DEP4 at 256/384/512 and R10 DEP8 at 1024, includes a fixed-workspace comparator, and measures service metrics and KV capacity. It keeps custom and AIPerf strict goodput separate. Paired runs still need an explicit freeze of the request stream, cache hits, checkpoint, precision, flags, image digest, and DSpark state; proposed acceptance thresholds must be set before testing.

objections: PR #62073 does not report a decode performance result; absence of a result cannot be stated as a reported no-gain finding.
PR #62073 says the decode workspace adds an allocation and warmup, but the B200 KV capacity cost is unknown.
The archived `dspark_config=off` and refreshed k5 recipe conflict; neither is an established control configuration.
reviews.required_revision: Replace “The PR reports no decode gain” with “PR #62073 reports no decode performance measurement.” Label its workspace behavior as an author claim until the complete implementation and deployed backend are inspected. Specify the frozen run configuration and separately report R7b custom goodput 6.6288 and AIPerf strict goodput 4.6727.

improvement_path.rationale: Backend and knob inspection is a cheap eligibility check. If a legal control exists and profiling shows contention during shared-expert/combine overlap, comparison with the best fixed setting can test deployment value. An unmeasured bottleneck is an appropriate first falsification question.

legal_correct_integration.rationale: The proposed collective-order, stream-dependency, and graph-replay checks are appropriate, but no supplied evidence identifies the active B200 combine backend or establishes a legal CTA/SM resource knob. The paper's COMET control cannot establish that precondition for this backend.

source_support.rationale: The supplied paper conclusion says it “selects the communication-CTA count and the compute/communication resource partition before kernel launch” and places its evaluation on four A100 GPUs; its future-work passage expressly leaves newer GPUs and decode untested. PR #52781 reports about 9.7 µs of overlap on GB300. These are author reports, while B200 benefit is explicitly a transfer inference. The excerpted paper text and PR do not provide active-backend engineering evidence or a legal knob.

controlled_experiment.rationale: The design includes the specified R7b and R10 points, a best-legal-fixed-setting comparator, an overlap diagnostic where supported, serving metrics, quality, and KV capacity. Tuning and held-out traces are separated. The historical flags and image must be recovered or the baselines rerun under frozen, matched controls.

objections: The supplied paper passage supports launch-time resource selection in COMET on A100, not a B200 shared-expert/combine implementation.
PR #52781 reports overlap on a GB300 DeepEP v2 deployment; it does not identify the active B200 backend or expose a CTA/SM knob.
The paper extract has gaps, so detailed method and limitations beyond the quoted conclusion remain unknown.
reviews.required_revision: Keep H2 conditional. Before implementation, document the resolved B200 backend, the exact supported resource control and range, and evidence that shared-expert/combine work overlaps and contends for resources. Freeze matched baseline controls, then compare with the best fixed legal setting.

global_gaps: The active engine, precision, MoE and combine backends, FlashInfer version, MTP/DSpark state, runtime flags, and image digest are unknown.
The archive's `dspark_config=off` conflicts with the refreshed k5 recipe; historical and refreshed results cannot be treated as one matched baseline.
Actual cache-hit rate is unknown; the 75% cacheability target is not a measurement.
Neither a B200 decode workspace effect nor a B200 communication resource-selection effect has been measured in the supplied material.
No GPU work was performed in this review; later bounded experiments are consistent with the session constraint.
